I have farmed these 9 mu for 45 years, and at 59 I know exactly what my land and my back can handle. With only three of us at home and some family working off-farm, I must be careful with labor. Cotton pays well, but it is a tyrant—twelve or thirteen sprays for bollworm, hand weeding, and picking that bends you for weeks. So I will keep my cotton to 3.5 mu, planted with the improved jinmian4 seed I trust. The remaining 5.5 mu will go to spring maize with hybrid seed; maize is kinder to an old woman. I will no-till the maize to save diesel and time, but I must rotary-till the cotton bed to keep it clean. Both crops will get compound fertilizer at sowing and a topdress of urea when the maize joints and the cotton flowers. I have my well, so I will irrigate three times for each when the summer drought comes. The maize will need only herbicide and a spray or two for corn borer—four times in all. The cotton will need spraying almost every week through July and August. I expect about 200 kg of grain per mu from the maize and about 170 kg of seed cotton per mu. That will feed us, cover the costs, and leave a little for my grandson's schooling.
